decisions.statement: PAF is a portable engineering-campaign assurance and control layer, not an agent or workflow framework.
Implementation is organized as paf.kernel, paf.control, paf.assurance, plus namespaced domain profiles.
Accepted semantic history is append-only; bootstrap uses atomic files and reusable core uses SQLite WAL plus immutable blobs.
The ledger is authoritative; the Semantic Work Graph and other graph views are derived projections.
All adaptive behavior follows a bounded propose-validate-critique-accept-execute-assess-repair protocol.
Execution requests capabilities and creates an exact RouteBinding; fallback and switching are never silent.
AssessmentProtocol is immutable and versioned, with validation and experiment profiles.
Candidate work cannot modify or silently influence evaluator assets, baseline, benchmark, parser, or promotion policy.
Search and evolution algorithms are adapters, not PAF core engines.
Candidate lineage is an optional campaign profile.
Protected completion requires exact-subject independent assessment according to an IndependencePolicy.
One PackageManifest supports Audit, Evidence, Reproduction, and Completion profiles.
Tools use tiered mediation; protected effects require fresh commit-time authorization and receipts.
MCP, A2A, OpenTelemetry, OPA, and in-toto/SLSA are adapters/standards, not authority by themselves.
Backend order is current Cline/local semantics, OpenHands portability, LangGraph adaptation, then Temporal when required.
Persistence migration is staged; no bootstrap-wide SQLite rewrite precedes stable contracts.
Every agent attempt references an immutable ContextPackage and retrieval provenance.
Audit records explicit engineering rationale and evidence, not hidden chain-of-thought.
Retry, task revision, prerequisite resolution, regeneration, recovery, reconciliation, and replanning are distinct.
Domain profiles are namespaced and cannot override kernel identity or protected invariants.
Autonomous loops cannot weaken safety, evaluator integrity, correctness, or protected approval policy.
Standalone extraction follows stable APIs, recovery/packages, a second runtime, and one real EvolveHLS campaign.
Semantic contracts, interchange encoding, and canonical bytes are separate normative layers.
Schema/version negotiation, unknown fields, migration, and source lineage are explicit and tested.
Every active phase has durable controller-owned run identity; old logs are never inferred active by recency alone.
Protected durable effects are reauthorized at commit time against current dependencies and eligibility.
External effects declare idempotency and reconciliation semantics.
Error and block taxonomies determine permitted recovery actions.
Budgets are multidimensional and explicit; bootstrap begins with time, attempts, tokens/cost, and tool timeouts.
RAG is a replaceable deterministic-first context adapter; no retrieval framework is authoritative.
Conformance tests accompany every contract slice.
Bootstrap implementation choices are temporary unless mapped explicitly to reusable PAF contracts.
